summary_paraphrase: A child plays find-the-carrot with Pig, who finds it under the broom. The next morning Pig's sty is empty; the child is comforted, searches all day and says how much they miss their friend. Pig returns with three piglets, the game starts again with all of them, and the day ends with goodnight at the sty.

beats.function: Pig searches; not here, not there
child misses Pig; picture reveals Pig and piglets

characters.name: the child (unnamed)
characters.weakness: cannot find Pig; Pig returns on her own
characters.change: from loss to a bigger family of friends

characters.name: Pig
characters.desire: never stated; inferred: a safe place to give birth

humor_notes: Little humor; gentle animal behaviour (Pig searching under the tub, a piglet on the ladder). OBSERVED

repetition.description: The praise for Pig returns at the found carrot and at the reunion
repetition.why: the reunion echoes the first game, so the listener feels the friendship restored

repetition.description: The invitation to play opens the book, is repeated at the empty sty and returns for all the pigs
repetition.why: the same invitation marks ordinary day, loss and return; its third use includes the new piglets

repetition.description: Two parallel negatives during the search; a one-two-three count of the new friends
repetition.why: very short, sayable patterns for the youngest listeners

notes: The picture tells the secret before the text: on page 7 Pig and her piglets stand hidden in the bushes while the child sits missing her. OBSERVED
Why Pig left (to have piglets) is never said; it can only be inferred from the pictures. INFERRED
The adult's comfort (child on a lap, arm around her) on page 5 is picture-only. OBSERVED
Objects form a circle: tub, broom, carrot and sty return from the first spreads in the last ones. OBSERVED
A single warm watercolour palette throughout, broken once by the dark night spread at the end. OBSERVED
Much white space; most spreads have one or two figures and a short line, giving quiet pages. OBSERVED

strengths: an extremely short text (68 words, longest sentence 6) that still carries loss and return
dramatic irony carried entirely by one picture
a circular ending at the sty, with the first game replayed by more players
a sad middle that is named in a plain sentence and comforted in the picture
a calm, dark last spread for a goodnight
weaknesses: the child does not find Pig; Pig simply comes back
the reason for the absence depends on reading the pictures; read aloud without them, the piglets appear unexplained
the child and the adult are unnamed

anti_patterns.note: The child searches but the return is Pig's doing, not hers. INFERRED

child_appeal_heuristic.label: Research heuristic — not validated
child_appeal_heuristic.rationale: Scores are the analyst's reading of the pages, not observations of children.

age_suitability.notes: A pet goes missing for a day and comes back with young; sadness is brief and comforted. No peril; birth is implied only by the piglets. INFERRED

metrics.lexicon_note: direct_address and sound_words are lexicon counts: a floor, not a measure. direct_address counts second-person words anywhere, dialogue included — it is not narrator-to-reader address

repetition.end_rhyme_note: heuristic: consecutive lines sharing a final two letters
